title: SPA/409/2014 of State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER Vs Anil Kumar AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 409 of 2014
State of Uttarakhand and others ....... Appellants
 versus
Anil Kumar and another ....... Respondents

Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel present for the appellant State.
Mr. Lok Pal Singh, Advocate with Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate present for
respondent no. 1.
Mr. B.S. Bisht, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate
present for respondent no. 2.
Coram : Hon'ble V.K. Bist, A.C.J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
 Advertisement no. 1/104/2010 was published
for filling up of 106 posts of Instructor (Arts /
Mathematics). Out of these posts, 23 posts were
reserved for Scheduled Caste category candidates.
Petitioner (respondent no. 1 herein) applied for the post
of Instructor (Arts / Mathematics) and participated in
the selection process. His name did not figure in the
select list of 23 posts. However, his name figured in
the waiting list at sl. no. 2 under the Scheduled Caste
category. Out of 23 candidates, only 19 candidates
joined as Instructor under the Scheduled Caste
category, and remaining posts were kept vacant. Offer
was given to the selected candidates by way of notice
dated 16.12.2012, published in Amar Ujala, to join the
said posts of Instructor, but four candidates did not join.
Consequently, four posts of Scheduled Caste category

2
remained vacant. Petitioner's prayer for giving him
appointment was declined, therefore, he filed writ
petition no. 423 (S/S) of 2013. The same was disposed
of by directing the respondent no. 2 to take action in
accordance with law on the select list. The
representation of the petitioner was rejected, against
which writ petition no. 1979 (S/S) of 2013 was filed.
The claim of the petitioner was that since four posts of
Scheduled Caste category are vacant, he should have
been offered appointment, as his name figured at sl. no.
2 of the waiting list.
2) In the counter affidavit, respondent
(appellant herein) came up with a case that appointment
could have been given to the petitioner only upto the
period of one year, as the waiting list survives for one
year and does not survive beyond such period and, in
the instant case, since one more year has elapsed,
therefore, petitioner cannot be offered appointment.
3) Learned Single Judge considered the contentions
of the petitioner as well as the respondent. By referring
the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in
State of J & K and others vs Satpal, rendered in Civil
Appeal no. 938-939 of 2013, the learned Single Judge
held that the period of limitation for one year for the
waiting list stars from the date when entire select list
has been filled up. Learned Single Judge observed that,
in the present case, last offer was given to the selected

3
candidate by way of notice dated 16.12.2012 and,
therefore, the period of one year has not expired.
Learned Single Judge allowed the writ petition and
issued mandamus to the respondents to give
appointment to the petitioner, as early as possible, but
definitely within six weeks from the date of production
of certified copy of the order.
4) Learned Standing Counsel submitted before us
that learned Single Judge failed to consider the fact that
where rules do not provide for waiting list, no
appointment can be given to that person whose name
figured in the waiting list. He relied upon the judgment
given by Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Rishi Mehra and
others vs State of Punjab and another, AIR 2013
Supreme Court 3580, in which Hon'ble Supreme Court
has held that where rules do not provide for the waiting
list, no direction can be issued to make appointment in
respect of a person whose name figured in the waiting
list.
5) While hearing the present case, we have perused
the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent in
the writ petition. In the said counter affidavit, it was
submitted that the claim of the petitioner for
appointment from the waiting list is not tenable in view
of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj
Rishi Mehra and others vs State of Punjab and another,
AIR 2013 Supreme Court 3580. But, in the counter

4
affidavit, it has not been pleaded by the respondents
that no rule exists for preparing the waiting list. Rather,
we find that the respondents themselves came up with
the case that life of waiting list is one year and since
one year has expired, the petitioner could not be given
appointment. Thus, the argument advanced by learned
Standing Counsel is contrary to what the State has
pleaded in their counter affidavit.
6) We do not find anything on the basis of which
the judgment of learned Single Judge can be set aside.
7) The special appeal thus stands dismissed.
8) Interim relief application no. 8728 of 2014 also
stands disposed of.

(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (V.K. Bist, A.C.J.)
Dt. November 10, 2014.
Negi
